task_instance: Simulate a 'Noob Mode' assisted session for a non-technical user: activate the skill, present a plain-English step plan, request approval (with WHAT/WHY/RISK/approve-decline blocks and color-coded risk icons) before reading contracts/memo.md, before editing it to add a deadline line, and before running git status/diff; translate the git output ('M' -> Modified) into plain English; and end with a completion summary (files changed + undo instructions).
evidence: Built a sample project at project/ (git-initialized, contracts/memo.md committed). Performed the real actions the skill narrates: read memo.md, edited it (added 'Deadline: final review comments due Friday, October 3, 2026'), ran `git status --short` and `git diff` to confirm the change. Wrote session_transcript.md containing the full noob-mode narration following every rule in SKILL.md: activation message, 3-step plain-English plan (Rule 4), approval blocks with WHAT/WHY/RISK/approve/decline for the read, edit, and shell-command actions (Rule 1) using the correct risk icons/levels from the Rule 2 table (🟢 Low for read, 🟡 Moderate for edit, 🔴 High-but-safe for git commands), jargon defined in parentheses on first use (Rule 3: 'time machine' for git, 'diff', 'Modified'), translated git status code M -> 'Modified' (Rule 5), and a final 'ALL DONE' summary listing files changed and an undo command (Rule 7). Verified programmatically with grep that every required section marker (WHAT I'M ASKING TO DO, WHY:, RISK:, If you approve, If you decline, HERE'S MY PLAN, Step 1 done, THAT WORKED, KEY DETAILS, ALL DONE, TO UNDO, and all three risk-color emojis) is present in session_transcript.md, and confirmed via `git status --short`/`git log`/`cat` that the underlying file edit genuinely occurred (one modified file, matching diff). Deliverable files: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec_ext/github__awesome-copilot__noob-mode/session_transcript.md and .../project/contracts/memo.md.
